A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SLIM and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Inspection covers all 17 pages of v1, including Appendices A–F, and all 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A–S. Renamed methods and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on OPT and LLaMA-2, including downstream accuracy, WikiText-2 perplexity, timing measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds comparator results, calibration and sparsity experiments, and broader GPU timing measurements.

M1.justification: The core quantizer, pruning pipeline, and saliency-based SVD construction remain. Adapter quantization changes from 16×16 AbsMax tiles containing 256 elements in v1 Section 3.4 to 128-element groups in v2 Section 3.3. v2 also introduces STE-based fine-tuning of quantized adapters; renaming the existing adapters SLIM-LoRA is not itself a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds SlimPajama as an alternative calibration corpus in Appendix O, Table 19. C4, the six downstream evaluation tasks, and WikiText-2 remain. Additional model sizes and GPU configurations expand experimental settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with AWQ, OmniQuant, AffineQuant, L2QER, and JSQ adapted to 4-bit quantization, substantially broadening the combined-compression and quantization-only comparisons. Earlier non-group AbsMax/OPTQ configurations are removed or replaced in the corresponding tables. Wanda-SVD/SVD matches Naive-LoRA or SLIM-Naive rather than constituting a new comparator.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates 4-bit weights with 8-bit group-quantized activations; v2 specifies weight-only quantization. Fine-tuning documentation changes from AdamW/H100 to AdaFactor/A100, although the retained timing table still specifies H100. New designs include matched-budget comparisons, 2-bit quantization versus 4-bit sparse compression, and timing across batch sizes 16/32/64 and larger LLaMA layer configurations. These reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds equal-memory model comparisons, sparsity-versus-bitwidth experiments, calibration-corpus sensitivity, sparsity-ratio sensitivity, and group-quantization overhead measurements (Figure 2 and Appendices G, O, P, S). Memory/FLOP accounting also expands the efficiency analysis. The earlier pruning-only, quantization-only, adapter-rank, and calibration-sample analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. Both present point estimates and sensitivity curves without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Accuracy and perplexity tables are extensively revised, and new comparator, trade-off, robustness, and hardware results are added. For example, LLaMA-2-7B SLIM accuracy under 2:4 sparsity changes from 50.8 in v1 Table 1 to 51.15 in v2 Table 1; the changed activation-quantization protocol prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. Pruning-only accuracy and compression-time results are largely retained.

T1.justification: Appendices J–K add explicit whole-model memory and FLOP reduction formulas beyond v1's per-layer asymptotic adapter-cost analysis. The principal quantization and saliency/SVD derivations remain substantially unchanged. v2 additionally asserts a convex reformulation in the introduction without supplying a corresponding convexity proof.

C1.justification: v2 adds central claims about shifting the accuracy–size Pareto frontier and outperforming dense models at equal bit budgets, alongside explicit RTX 3060/A100 speedup claims. It also newly claims that the probabilistic formulation makes quantization optimization convex. v1 emphasizes accuracy recovery and inexpensive fine-tuning without these broader claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning model selection under memory budgets, sparsity versus bitwidth, calibration-corpus insensitivity, and usable sparsity levels. The earlier limitation about unavailable group-quantized sparse kernels is revised through discussion of Marlin implementation constraints and measured small-model slowdowns on A100 GPUs. These materially expand the paper's applicability and failure-condition discussion.

D1.justification: v2 documents the histogram-bin selection rule, baseline group size of 128, explicit adapter-rank default, Triton kernels for quantized-adapter fine-tuning, and Marlin/vLLM/PyTorch inference choices. It also revises optimizer and GPU descriptions. These substantially expand implementation information, although the A100 fine-tuning description and retained H100 timing documentation are not clearly reconciled. The code/data access URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 introduces a dedicated related-work appendix and substantially expands positioning against L2QER, JSQ, modern quantizers, and inference systems. Added references include OmniQuant, AffineQuant, QuaRot, LLM.int8(), LoRA, and Marlin. The discussion more explicitly distinguishes SLIM's combined sparsity/quantization and adapter treatment from prior approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial method explanations are rewritten; contribution bullets become an extended narrative. Pruning-only, quantization-only, and fine-tuning-cost discussions move into reorganized appendices, and adapter terminology changes throughout. The title, author list, conclusion structure, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive table restructuring and relocation. v2 adds accuracy-versus-size and sparsity plots, a multipanel GPU speedup figure, and additional analysis tables. The earlier sensitivity figure is retained with revised labels/colors, while the original compact speedup table is replaced by broader displays.

improvement.justification: The added L2QER and modern-quantizer comparisons, robustness analyses, and concrete GPU profiling improve assessment of SLIM beyond v1's narrower evidence. However, stronger claims introduce reporting weaknesses: the convexity assertion lacks a supporting proof, and the abstract's RTX 3060 maximum of 3.78× does not match Table 3's 3.99×. Together with unclear fine-tuning hardware documentation, these issues limit the overall quality gain.
